gap: No result ChatGPT got states a yearly electricity cost for a specific model. We worked out about $11.14 a year for the UGREEN DXP2800 (ocinside measured about 7 W at idle) and about $17.50 a year for the TerraMaster F2-424 (TerraMaster's 11.0 W figure with drives hibernating), both at EIA's US average residential rate for August 2026 of 18.16¢/kWh.
standout_why: Starry Hope's 'Best 2-Bay NAS' page has only a general rule of about 88 kWh, or about $16, per year for every 10 W at about 18¢/kWh. Its one measured idle figure is Notebookcheck's for the DXP2800 GT, a $459.99 model that is over budget. It gives no yearly cost for the DXP2800, F2-424 or F2-425 Plus. ComputingForGeeks' QuickSync picks page says it is 'a spec and capability guide, not a bench test' and has no wattage or stream counts. Jellyfin's Hardware Selection page has no power or stream figures. So the rivals have the method but not the numbers for each model.
decides: This confirms the DXP2800 pick rather than changing it. At idle the cheapest and dearest candidates differ by only about $6 a year, and even the DXP2800 running flat out all year (34.7 W) would cost about $55. Running cost should not swing the choice. The pick rests on the N100's Quick Sync, which Jellyfin's docs recommend by name, and on the purchase price.
